results.name: numeric_neighbor_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for targets 1-5 away from the nearest example that share no last digit with any example, among sets whose examples span more than 20; observed > null means people use raw numerical similarity beyond what rules and a single interval predict, observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: numeric_neighbor_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate for targets 1-5 away from the nearest example that share no last digit with any example, among sets whose examples span more than 20; observed > null means people use raw numerical similarity beyond what rules and a single interval predict, observed < null means less.
def _parse(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    return ex, t

def test_statistic(df):
    ex, t = _parse(df)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    d = np.where(valid, np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.inf).min(axis=1)
    span = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1) - np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    share_digit = (valid & (np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10 == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    m = (d >= 1) & (d <= 5) & ~share_digit & (span > 20)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: cell_response_consistency
results.description: Mean over repeated (set,target) cells (2+ responses) of the within-cell Bernoulli variance p(1-p) of yes responses; observed < null means people agree with each other more (more deterministic answers) than the model's intermediate probabilities imply, observed > null means more disagreement.
results.code:
# name: cell_response_consistency
# description: Mean over repeated (set,target) cells (2+ responses) of the within-cell Bernoulli variance p(1-p) of yes responses; observed < null means people agree with each other more (more deterministic answers) than the model's intermediate probabilities imply, observed > null means more disagreement.
def test_statistic(df):
    key = df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(str)
    g = df["rating"].astype(float).groupby(key)
    p = g.mean(); c = g.size()
    p = p[c >= 2]
    return float((p * (1 - p)).mean()) if len(p) else 0.0

results.name: near_outside_range_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for targets outside [min,max] of the examples but within 10 of that range (excluding targets sharing a last digit with an example), for sets of 2+ examples; observed > null means people extend numerical intervals beyond the examples more than the model, observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: near_outside_range_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate for targets outside [min,max] of the examples but within 10 of that range (excluding targets sharing a last digit with an example), for sets of 2+ examples; observed > null means people extend numerical intervals beyond the examples more than the model, observed < null means less.
def _parse(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    return ex, t

def test_statistic(df):
    ex, t = _parse(df)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    gap = np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi)
    share_digit = (valid & (np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10 == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & (gap > 0) & (gap <= 10) & ~share_digit
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: early_minus_late_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate on trials with trial_index < 90 minus yes-rate on later trials; observed > null means people say yes more early in the session than the static model predicts (a time-varying response bias the model lacks).

results.name: inside_range_nonrule_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for targets strictly inside [min,max] of 3-4 example sets, not equal to an example and sharing no last digit with any example; observed < null means the model over-predicts interval (filling-in) generalization, observed > null means people fill in ranges more than the model.

def _parse(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    return ex, t

def test_statistic(df):
    ex, t = _parse(df)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    share_digit = (valid & (np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10 == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(axis=1)

results.name: single_example_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate on trials whose set has exactly one example, minus the yes-rate on trials with 3-4 examples; observed > null means people generalize from one example relatively more broadly than the model's size principle predicts, observed < null means more narrowly.
results.code:
# name: single_example_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate on trials whose set has exactly one example, minus the yes-rate on trials with 3-4 examples; observed > null means people generalize from one example relatively more broadly than the model's size principle predicts, observed < null means more narrowly.
def _parse(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    return ex, t

def test_statistic(df):
    ex, t = _parse(df)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    a = n == 1; b = n >= 3
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: common_last_digit_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for targets (not in the set) whose last digit equals the last digit shared by all 2+ examples of the set; observed < null means people generalize a shared last digit less confidently than the model's near-certain "ends in d" rule, observed > null means more.
results.code:
# name: common_last_digit_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate for targets (not in the set) whose last digit equals the last digit shared by all 2+ examples of the set; observed < null means people generalize a shared last digit less confidently than the model's near-certain "ends in d" rule, observed > null means more.
def _parse(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    return ex, t

def test_statistic(df):
    ex, t = _parse(df)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    dig = np.where(valid, np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10, -1)
    first = dig[:, 0]
    all_same = ((dig == first[:, None]) | ~valid).all(axis=1)
    in_set = (valid & (np.nan_to_num(ex) == t[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & all_same & (t % 10 == first) & ~in_set
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: far_unrelated_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for targets >15 from every example, sharing no last digit with any example, and of a different parity than at least one example; observed > null means people say yes to unrelated targets more than the model (missing lapse/guessing), observed < null means the model over-generalizes.
results.code:
# name: far_unrelated_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate for targets >15 from every example, sharing no last digit with any example, and of a different parity than at least one example; observed > null means people say yes to unrelated targets more than the model (missing lapse/guessing), observed < null means the model over-generalizes.
def _parse(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    return ex, t

def test_statistic(df):
    ex, t = _parse(df)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    d = np.where(valid, np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.inf).min(axis=1)
    share_digit = (valid & (np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10 == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    par_diff = (valid & (np.nan_to_num(ex) % 2 != (t % 2)[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    m = (d > 15) & ~share_digit & par_diff
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0
